chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm if the one fearing [danger or difficulty] throws [the pebbles] at night, offers the sacrifice at night, and departs [from Mina] at night."

key_terms.الْخَائِفُ: The one fearing (a valid excuse for deviating from the standard Hajj schedule)
key_terms.يَرْمِيَ: He throws (referring to ramy al-jamarat, throwing pebbles at the pillars)
key_terms.يُضَحِّيَ: He offers the sacrifice (udhiyah, the ritual animal sacrifice)
key_terms.يُفِيضَ: He departs/moves (referring to ifaadah, the departure from Mina)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to throw the jamarat and sacrifice the animal at night during Hajj?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies that the night-time performance of throwing the jamarat, offering the sacrifice, and departing Mina is not merely an exception for the fearful but a general permissibility rooted in the flexibility of Sharia. It underscores the principle of *rukhsah* (concession), allowing pilgrims to ease their burden by performing these acts at night, thereby preventing congestion and facilitating the completion of Hajj obligations. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence for validating night rituals as fully compliant with the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams.
